# Stop Chatting. Start Delegating. {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

::: {data-id="reframe" style="background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
You don't need a chatbot. You need a **direct report** — brief it like you'd brief a new
hire.
:::

{{< include ../../chunks/_rice.qmd >}}

## Don't Ask — Delegate {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="example" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
**Don't ask:** "Write an email about the meeting."
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
**Delegate:** "Act as my chief of staff. Turn these meeting notes into a recap email to the
team — Summary, Decisions, Action Items with owners and deadlines. Flag anything that still
needs a decision."
:::
:::

## The RICE Prompt {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.7em;"}
**Role:** Act as my chief of staff.

**Instructions:** Turn these notes into a recap email to the team. Use headers — Summary,
Decisions, Action Items (Owner / Deadline), Open Questions. Keep it under 200 words. Put
deadlines in **bold**. If an item has no owner, list it under Open Questions.

**Context:** Notes from today's Q3 launch sync: *[paste notes]*

**Example:** Match this opening — *"Team — quick recap from today's sync and what's next: …"*
:::

## What Made It Work {auto-animate=true}

::: {.incremental}
- **Role** → wrote like a chief of staff, not a generic bot
- **Instructions** → fixed sections, length, tone, and the "no owner → Open Questions" rule
- **Context** → the messy notes were enough — the AI extracted the structure
- **Example** → matched your real opening line
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #00C9A7; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
Examples are the secret weapon — show it *one* good output and it copies the shape.
:::

{{< include ../../chunks/_advanced_moves.qmd >}}

## Match the Move to the Job {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
| The task | The move |
|---|---|
| Reconcile a budget / total a column | **Double-check** *(Self-Consistency)* |
| Work out a project timeline or logic | **Think step by step** *(Chain of Thought)* |
| "Should we pick vendor A or B?" | **Debate it out** *(Tree of Thoughts)* |
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
By default AI answers **fast and shallow** — these slow it down where it matters.
:::

{{< include ../../chunks/_newspaper_test.qmd >}}

## Safe vs. Risky — Spot It {auto-animate=true}

**You want to summarize a customer complaint email that names the customer and their account number.**

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #fff0ed; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
**Risky.** Strip the name and account number first — replace with "the customer / [ACCOUNT].
Then summarize. The AI doesn't need the identity to do the job.
:::
:::

# Build: Delegate a Real Task {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Your turn — pull one task from your backlog

## Write a Full RICE Delegation {auto-animate=true}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hands-on
1. Pick one recurring **"messy → clean"** task from your **Automation Backlog**.
2. Write a full **RICE** prompt for it — Role, Instructions (format / length / tone),
   Context, and one **Example** of the output you want.
3. Run it. Then add the matching **advanced move** to a numbers/judgment task
   (double-check / step by step / debate it out).
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## Newspaper Test first
Sanitize names, numbers, and secrets **before** you paste anything in.
:::

## Key Takeaways {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Delegate, don't ask** — brief the AI with **RICE** (Role, Instructions, Context, Examples)
2. **Context is the same thing** you mapped in the two-layers session
3. **Examples are the secret weapon** — show one good output and it copies the shape
4. **Slow it down on hard problems** — step by step, debate it out, double-check
5. **Newspaper Test first** — sanitize before you paste
:::
